title: Quarterly renewal readout and EU on-prem staging - Helixium Therapeutics
customer_attendees: Dr. Priya Nair - Head of ML
next_steps: Redwood to share updated SOW with staged capacity and pricing by 2027-03-08
Customer to schedule on-prem workshop for week of 2027-03-21
Run 48-hour throughput soak test on dedicated nodes (Redwood + Helixium)
action_items: Maya Chen: Draft amended contract / pricing table and send to Tomás (due 2027-03-08)
Liam Rodriguez: Prepare benchmarking script and config for Helixium on-prem pilot (due 2027-03-12)
Evan Cole: Collect current traffic profile (qps, p95 token length) and share CSV with Redwood (due 2027-03-07)
Linda Park: Confirm compliance docs needed (SOC2 type II points and KMS integration checklist) and email Redwood (due 2027-03-10)
header: Date: 2027-03-04 | Start: 15:05 UTC | Duration: 46m | Platform: Zoom | Recording: yes
summary: Check-in to review upcoming renewal, proposed capacity uplift, addition of EU on-prem staging for data residency, and contract amendment timeline. Discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, KMS/HSM integration, preliminary soak test plan, and next-step milestones.
topics: EU on-prem staging & data residency requirements
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll give folks a couple seconds to pop in. Uh this is Maya from Redwood, with Liam on the call too.
00:12 Tomás Ferreira: hey Maya, hi Liam, thanks. we have Dr. Priya and Linda and Evan on our side, so thanks for doing the readout.
00:22 Maya Chen: great. quick agenda — status on utilization, proposed uplift numbers, EU on-prem staging plan, security ask, then wrap with action items. Sound good?
00:30 Dr. Priya Nair: yep yep looks good.
00:34 Liam Rodriguez: quick note — I'll jump into the benchmarking bits later, got a rough config to show.
00:40 Tomás Ferreira: just so you know timeline for renewal is end of April, we'd like to finalize the amendment two weeks earlier ideally.
00:51 Maya Chen: perfect, so say by 2027-04-15 contract inked, provisioning shortly after. ok first: utilization — Evan do you want to summarize current qps and peak windows?
01:02 Evan Cole: yeah sure, so current avg qps 48, peak 170, p95 lat ~320ms on hosted endpoint, token lengths vary 40 to 220 depending on clinical note gen. we're seeing bursts during nightly ingest where everything spikes.
01:20 Dr. Priya Nair: and accuracy requirements haven't changed; the models are the same but traffic growth is projected 2.7x over next 12 months.
01:29 Maya Chen: thanks. so our suggested uplift is two things: a reserved dedicated pool for steady baseline and a small shared burst for peaks. proposal in the deck — baseline 8 reserved GPU slots (A100-style perf equiv), 30% burst capacity via hosted.
01:48 Tomás Ferreira: 8 nodes—that was the midcase we discussed earlier. Curious on cost delta vs keeping more hosted?
01:55 Liam Rodriguez: right, dedicated lowers per-token cost cause of continuous batching and cache reuse, but there's fixed monthly commit. For Helixium's forecast, dedicated baseline + hosted burst drops unit cost by approx 42% vs current pure hosted usage, even after the reserved monthly. caveat: quantization and perf tuning we'll do during pilot.
02:20 Linda Park: from security standpoint we need full audit logs, KMS integration and the EU data residency guarantee. We also need clarity on key rotation and whether Redwood can support our HSM via bring-your-own-key.
02:37 Maya Chen: absolutely. Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations — we have a BYOK path with HSM, and key rotation policies can be coordinated. we'll attach the tech note and integration checklist.
02:48 Dr. Priya Nair: question — for the EU on-prem staging what exactly is staged? Is it a full private control plane or just model serving?
02:56 Liam Rodriguez: good question. For the proposed pilot the control plane remains Redwood-managed in a private VPC region, but the inference nodes and storage for KV caches and prefixes will be customer-hosted in your EU datacenter — so inference execution + cache = on-prem, control plane metadata can stay in our private tenant region if that's acceptable for audit trail.
03:20 Tomás Ferreira: would that pass our legal team's data-in-transit checks?
03:24 Linda Park: we need to confirm network diagrams and egress policies, but sounds promising. Also we need assurance that no PII leaves EU during staging, so any telemetry that might contain patient identifiers must be redacted client-side.
03:39 Liam Rodriguez: we can support client-side redaction hooks and a no-telemetry mode for pilot. there will be tradeoffs on observability though — you lose some remote tracing.
03:50 Maya Chen: noted. next, soak test and acceptance criteria. Liam?
03:55 Liam Rodriguez: plan is a 48-hour throughput soak: synthetic traffic shaped by Evan's real profile. Targets: maintain p95 < 350ms for generation workloads at 2.7x projected load with 99.9% availability. We'll also measure token cost and KV cache hit rate. I'll share the script and the dockerized harness.
04:18 Tomás Ferreira: and who's running the soak — Redwood or Helixium?
04:21 Liam Rodriguez: joint run — Redwood will coordinate and run the harness, but Evan will provide the profile and the on-prem infra.
04:28 Evan Cole: i'll pull the traffic CSV and give you samples by Monday.
04:33 Linda Park: for compliance, we need audit logs retained for 2 years, and exportable in a particular format. Is that supported?
04:41 Maya Chen: Redwood Console supports exportable audit logs, retention policies can be extended as an add-on. We'll include retention options in the SOW.
04:49 Dr. Priya Nair: one more — model rollout strategy. We want canary first, then gradual rollout. Do you support automatic fallback to hosted model if on-prem fails?
04:59 Liam Rodriguez: yes, smart routing can fail back to a hosted-compatible variant. We'll propose a 5% canary then 25% then full if metrics look good, with automatic rollback if quality regressions or latency SLOs are violated.
05:15 Tomás Ferreira: competition aside — we've also talked with MegaCloud AI — their price was aggressive but they don't offer the same private on-prem tooling. It's a close call costwise.
05:28 Maya Chen: understood — we'll make the SOW clear on total cost of ownership, including ops time and the rollback safety net.
05:34 Linda Park: about KMS — can you confirm whether Redwood will hold any keys in hosted control plane in the pilot? we prefer zero-knowledge where possible.
05:44 Liam Rodriguez: for BYOK, customer keys remain in your HSM. Redwood only stores key references and never the raw material. For some control-plane ops we may request temporary wrapping keys but that can be scoped away for pilot.
05:58 Dr. Priya Nair: timeline check — we need pilot before end of Q2 to migrate EU customers by Q4. Is that doable?
06:07 Maya Chen: yes. timeline in bullets: SOW by 03-08, on-prem workshop week of 03-21, infra prep and provisioning in April, pilot run in May, production cutover and ramp Q3.
06:22 Tomás Ferreira: sounds good. any bigger risks we should call out?
06:26 Liam Rodriguez: risk: network egress misconfig, KV cache warm-up causing initial latency spike, and model quantization regressions if we push too aggressive. Mitigations: pre-warm cache, conservative quantization profile in pilot, and run regression evals on our eval harness.
06:46 Evan Cole: on the cache warm-up — do you have a recommended pre-warm period or approach?
06:50 Liam Rodriguez: typical is 12-24 hour synthetic warm-up prior to traffic ramp, and a rolling warm-up approach for canary. We'll add scripts for that.
07:01 Linda Park: legal will want a clause about data residency violation penalties for the pilot — can you accept a limited SLA with clear remediation steps?
07:10 Maya Chen: we can work with legal; we usually do a remediation playbook and crediting model instead of heavy penalties for pilot, but for production we can discuss stricter terms.
07:22 Dr. Priya Nair: okay good. any clarifying questions from Redwood?
07:25 Maya Chen: one — what's your internal decision process? who signs off post-pilot?
07:30 Tomás Ferreira: sign-off is Priya + Linda for security, and me for budget. Expect final sign-off within two weeks after the pilot if metrics are met.
07:40 Maya Chen: perfect. i'll recap in the follow up.
07:44 Liam Rodriguez: quick demo note — the harness will produce a benchmark sheet with p50/p95/p99, token cost, cache hit %. We'll template it so legal and eng can review quickly.
07:55 Evan Cole: i'll get you token length distribution by Monday as promised.
07:58 Linda Park: i'll compile the compliance checklist and highlight anything we need from Redwood re: audit schema.
08:06 Maya Chen: thanks Linda. ok wrapping — recap of next actions: SOW to Tomás by 03-08, benchmark harness and scripts to Evan and Priya by 03-12, on-prem workshop scheduling for 03-21 week, and retention/KMS docs attached.
08:23 Tomás Ferreira: thanks all, look forward to the SOW.
08:27 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
08:30 [meeting ends]
